auditMetadata.title: Specialist Planner v0.7.1 — Read-only Legacy Unit/Lesson Reconciliation Audit

provenanceTimeline.finding: Initial SP generation stored Program-owned Units/Lessons with stable SP IDs.
Setup directly supported adding, renaming, reordering and deleting Units and Lessons; new records used unit-/lesson- UUIDs.
TMR references became optional. Selecting a Unit reference preserved local SP Lessons; Lesson references were separately optional.
Live Unit selection began materialising complete TMR Units with stable Lesson references.

provenanceConclusion: The six 31-Lesson legacy Units are later Unit-linked SP-native records. Missing Lesson-level TMR IDs are historically expected, not proof of broken synchronization.

truthModel.curriculumLibraryTruth: Current TMR production Unit documents describe the present reusable curriculum/library sequence.
truthModel.currentOperationalTruth: SP revision 79 classProgress/year-level references describe where current classes are positioned, including active Family and Fruit legacy records.
truthModel.historicalTeachingTruth: SP Teaching Session snapshots remain immutable evidence of what was planned/taught under earlier SP-native sequences.

tmrLessons.title: Typing Chinese characters
tmrLessons.learningIntention: We are learning to or revisiting how to type Chinese characters using the Pinyin input method.
tmrLessons.notes:
Students learn to install and delete a keyboard on an iPad: Settings/General/Keyboards/Add a new keyboard/Chinese (Simplified)/Pinyin-QWERTY.
Students create a note in Notes on an iPad and type Chinese numbers, colours and countries, using the Pinyin input method.

tmrLessons.title: Homophones
tmrLessons.learningIntention:
We are learning to understand homophones are words that sound the same but don't write the same or have the same definitions.
Homophones make a common feature in the Chinese languages.
tmrLessons.notes:
1. Students write the following homophones in their book: 
yi：一，伊，衣，医
2. Students use an online dictionary to search the definition of each character and share their results and findings to the class.
3. Students practise and reinforce their typing skills and use of an online dictionary with another group of homophones:
si: 四，丝，斯，死
4. Students apply these skills and search the definition of characters used in their own Chinese names.

tmrLessons.title: My Chinese Name I
tmrLessons.learningIntention:
We are reinforcing our Chinese character typing skills.
We are applying our typing skills when finding definition of characters used in our Chinese names.
tmrLessons.notes:
Students share the definition of their Chinese names to their partner and class.
Students create a digital bookmark on Canva, including their Chinese name (characters & Pinyin) and definition.

tmrLessons.title: My Chinese Name II
tmrLessons.learningIntention: We are learning to ask each other names in a mini dialogue.
tmrLessons.notes:
Students listen to a song and revise asking each other names through singing practice.
Students apply the core and challenge practice to conduct mini dialogue with their partner.
Students write their Chinese and English names on 4 pieces of paper to make 4 small business cards. They walk around in the room to find 4 partners and conduct the mini dialogue and exchange business cards with each other.
Students continue to finalise their Chinese name bookmark and submit their task.

tmrLessons.title: Mini Self-introduction I

tmrLessons.notes:

tmrLessons.title: There are five people in my family.
tmrLessons.learningIntention:
We are revising family words from Year 2.
We are learning to use the counter word 个 when counting people.
We are learning to describe how many people there are in our family.
tmrLessons.notes:
1. Warm Up - Mini Whiteboard 
Students practise writing basic Chinese characters with the teacher: 一～十, 人, 个, 大, 太, 天, 女生，男生，女人，男人, *family words
2. Use 个 when counting people
我家有五个人。
3. Speaking Practice - Business Cards
Students walk around to practise the core sentence with their peers.
4. Share
谁家有四个人？谁家有五个人？哈德森家有几个人？丽丽家有几个人？
5. Apply
Students write a sentence about their own family in their books.

year2FamilyConclusion.conclusion: The evidence strongly suggests TMR Family Tree II was inserted into the current TMR sequence after or independently of the four-Lesson SP-native sequence. SP L3 corresponds as a candidate to TMR L4 by exact distinctive title, not to TMR L3. TMR L3 must not be mapped to SP L3.
reasonsTmrL3IsNotSpL3: TMR L3 is Family Tree II; SP L3 is My family has five people.
SP L3 has an exact distinctive-title candidate at TMR L4.
The old SP editor allowed independent Lesson authoring and the Family Unit has no Lesson provenance IDs.
Array position is explicitly non-authoritative and the structure is 4 SP Lessons versus 5 TMR Lessons.

migrationBlockers.issue: Six SP-native Units have no Lesson provenance contract.
Family, Fruit, Countries and Australian States have structural divergence (insertions, extensions or possible splits).
Historically referenced SP Lessons cannot be deleted or replaced without orphaning operational/history references.
Title/position similarity is candidate evidence only and cannot create identity.
Two distinct TMR Unit IDs use similar Australia/States naming but represent different current Units.
TMR-only Lessons need owner decisions on whether they are new curriculum, split content or future-only extensions.

provenanceVsDivergenceVsDefect.provenanceProblem: Legacy Lessons lack evidence of TMR origin because they were SP-native and linked later at Unit level.
provenanceVsDivergenceVsDefect.curriculumDivergence: Several current TMR sequences have evolved beyond the older SP-native operational sequences.
provenanceVsDivergenceVsDefect.synchronizationDefect: No synchronization defect was demonstrated for these legacy Lessons. The Family II hotfix behaves correctly where stable Lesson IDs exist; refusing to reconcile unmapped legacy Lessons is expected safety behaviour.

futureApproaches.description: Backfill TMR provenance only for owner-approved, clearly matched SP Lessons.
advantages: Enables safe future metadata reconciliation for approved pairs.
risks: Splits/reorders require more than one-to-one IDs.

futureApproaches.description: Use an explicit one-time mapping table during authority migration without writing provenance onto every legacy Lesson first.
advantages: Keeps audit decisions explicit and reversible before migration.
risks: Mapping table still requires owner approval.

futureApproaches.description: Preserve SP-native Lessons as historical operational records and create new SP-authoritative curriculum Lessons separately.
advantages: Avoids pretending new curriculum is identical to old teaching records.
risks: Requires a clear active-vs-legacy lifecycle model.
Current class transitions need explicit checkpoints.

futureApproaches.description: Use a Unit-specific hybrid of A/B/C.
advantages: Fits the materially different provenance and divergence patterns.
risks: Requires per-Unit owner decisions and engineering safeguards.

shouldLegacyLessonsReceiveTmrIds: Not categorically. Provenance IDs should only be backfilled for owner-approved pairs whose historical identity is established by multiple signals. Structurally divergent SP-native Lessons should remain historical operational records or be handled by an explicit migration table/lifecycle model.

familyIIHotfixBoundary.appropriateFor: New-style linked Units with stable Unit and Lesson IDs, such as Family II and the four 3 Oct imports.
familyIIHotfixBoundary.inappropriateFor: SP-native legacy Lessons without stable Lesson provenance IDs.
familyIIHotfixBoundary.year2FamilyCause: B — expected limitation caused by missing legacy Lesson identity and structural divergence, not a Family II reconciliation defect.

noModificationConfirmation: No SP/TMR data, source code, mappings, Firebase rules, Storage, deployment or backups were modified. Only these two local audit reports were generated.
